messages:
jenn_customer: hitting intermittent 401s during a long streaming request (SSE). stream opens fine, then after ~30-90s we get an Authorization failure and the stream closes. logged x-request-id: req_9f7a2c. headers from client show Authorization present. can provide curl repro if you need it.

sasha_support: thanks jenn — that req id helps. before a full debug bundle, can you run a minimal curl repro and grab response headers? worst-case we ask for a pcap.

jenn_customer: sure. here's the simplified curl i used (redacted API key):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -N "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=gpt-rr"
```
response eventually returns a 401 and a short body: `{"error":"unauthorized"}`. headers include `x-request-id: req_9f7a2c` and `date: Tue, 07 Jun 2026 14:22:11 GMT`.

eric_eng: quick checklist:
- confirm the token in curl is exactly the same as the app is using (double-check no extra whitespace).
- add `--dump-header hdrs.txt` to capture server headers.
- run with `-v` to capture TLS handshake logs.
If you can share hdrs.txt and the terminal output we'll inspect token scope/expiry and any auth middleware messages.

mira_infra: also ask for `--no-buffer`/`-N` (you already have -N) and try adding `-H "X-REDWOOD-TRACE: 1"` so backend emits trace ids. that header is safe to send. it will show up in request logs as x-trace-id.

jenn_customer: running now with dumps:
```
curl -v -N --dump-header hdrs.txt -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "X-REDWOOD-TRACE: 1" \n  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=gpt-rr" 2> curl_verbose.txt
```
I got 401 at ~55s. hdrs.txt attached (redacted). curl_verbose shows TLS resumed, no obvious client-side timeout. the body still has `{"error":"unauthorized"}`; also found header `x-request-id: req_9f7a2c` and `x-trace-id: trace_44b`.

sasha_support: perfect — can you upload hdrs.txt and curl_verbose.txt to the secure upload link: https://upload.redwood.example/safe/XXXXX (expires in 24h). we'll pull the server-side logs for req_9f7a2c and trace_44b.

support-bot: Uploaded artifacts will be scanned for secrets. Please confirm API keys are redacted.

jenn_customer: uploaded. keys redacted. link: https://upload.redwood.example/safe/XXXXX/view

eric_eng: saw the bundle. server traces show an auth revocation event from the token introspection service at approx 14:22:10 UTC — same time as the stream drop. two theories: (1) token TTL/rotation on client side, (2) an intermediate proxy revalidating tokens for long-lived connections. can you confirm whether you have a token refresh job that might be replacing credentials mid-stream?

jenn_customer: we do rotate tokens every 45 minutes but rotation runs out-of-process and shouldn't touch in-flight connections. app logs show no refresh attempt at 14:22.

mira_infra: next step for confidence: capture a short pcap during a repro to see whether there is an active TCP reset or a 401 coming from the upstream immediately after a keepalive. if you're able to run ephemeral capture, command: `sudo tcpdump -i any -w redwood_stream.pcap host api.redwood.example and port 443` while reproducing. 30s capture should be enough.

sasha_support: if pcap isn't possible, we can request extended server-side debug: add header `X-REDWOOD-DUMP: true` for one repro and we'll persist the full request/response lifecycle (will include KV cache events). only use on repro we control.

jenn_customer: can do but need to coordinate — I'm in EU region and have compliance concerns. is there PII in server bundle?
\mira_infra: server bundle will redact payloads by default and only include metadata + internal trace events. nothing user-visible will be dumped unless explicitly requested. we can also mask the trace and share a summary.

eric_eng: we've correlated similar incidents to a proxy that enforces short token grace window for long-lived streaming. if your infra uses a CDN or L7 proxy (Cloudfront/NGINX ingress) in front of Redwood, please note which one. can you provide the `via` or `x-forwarded-for` from hdrs.txt?

jenn_customer: hdrs.txt shows `via: 1.1 varnish` and `x-forwarded-for: 10.0.4.2`. we do have Varnish in front of our client gateway.

sasha_support: ok that points to work on both sides. next concrete step: please run a focused repro with these exact steps and attach artifacts: headers dump, curl verbose, and either pcap or a short application log showing token state. use the same command but add `-H "X-REDWOOD-DUMP: true"` so we can request the server bundle when you upload.

jenn_customer: will run in ~30m and upload. thanks for the clear checklist.

sasha_support: thanks — we'll standby. once uploaded we'll pull server logs for req_9f7a2c/trace_44b and coordinate with infra to look at proxy idle/refresh behavior. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Reminder: do not paste full API keys into Slack. Artifacts will be scanned and auto-redacted on upload.
